correctness.rationale: For n>=3 the admissible upper indices are exactly 1<=k<=floor(beta n). With t={n alpha}, s_k={k alpha}, the identities alpha^2=beta and v(k)=2k+floor(k alpha) give {v(k)alpha}=beta s_k. Lower Beatty membership is {t-beta s_k}>beta. For t<beta this is the wrap condition s_k>t/beta, for beta<t<2beta it is s_k<(t-beta)/beta, and for t>2beta it holds for all k. Neither breakpoint occurs by irrationality. On length-q Fibonacci convergent blocks a translated rational q-grid differs by less than one grid spacing; only O(1) points near interval endpoints can change membership. Decomposing any length into O(log n) such blocks proves the uniform interval discrepancy. Hence Y_n is within O(log n/n) of the piecewise-linear tent-with-plateau profile, and equals one exactly on the plateau. On each dyadic block and uniformly in y<1, indicator disagreement is confined to at most two nonplateau intervals of total length O(log n/n); discrepancy gives O(log n) possible indices there. Summation proves the uniform log-squared estimate. Taking y up to 1 from below at fixed X and using the same uniform error immediately gives the stated exact-saturation count, independently of the separate proof of that count. Weak convergence and convergence of the stated moments follow. A new check compared 1798 direct pair counts with interval-certified rotation counts (python3 /workspace/branches/recompute_frozen.py); it does not certify the asymptotics.

evidence: Write t={n alpha}. In baee5a907c94 the exact count is the number of m in 1..n-1 with y={m alpha}>=beta and {t-y}<beta. When t>2 beta, every upper summand u=n-m has s={u alpha}<beta, so y={t-s}=t-s>beta. Thus the earlier exact rule gives r(n)=K(n) identically on the plateau.

Its uniform r(n)=n Lambda(t)+O(log n) gives |Y_n-Lambda(t)/beta|=O(log n/n). On a dyadic block of size at most 2^j, disagreement of a threshold y<1 with the profile can only occur off the exact plateau. There the profile has slopes of magnitude 1/beta, so the two affected intervals have combined length O((j+1)/2^j). The earlier translated-grid discrepancy gives O(j+1) possible indices in those intervals. Summing yields O(log^2(X+2)); the ideal threshold preimage has length 2 beta y, with O(log(X+2)) discrepancy.

For each fixed finite X, let y increase to 1 through values below 1 in that uniform estimate. The left count becomes the number with Y_n<1. Taking its complement proves the exact-saturation estimate with the same error.

Weak convergence alone would not suffice at the atom, but the exact interval criterion removes that obstruction. No distinct surviving theorem in the frozen statement warrants a repair.

Its proof supplies the exact circle-interval rule and uniform Fibonacci rotation discrepancy. This is established equivalent and implied coverage, not an inference from source titles, dates alone or inaccessible literature.
